title: Broken Blade
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: In a world where people power quartz machines with their minds, Rygart Arrow is one of the few who cannot, until he finds an ancient golem only he can pilot (CMX and Titan blurbs via AniList and MU). His old school friends King Hodr and Queen Sigyn need him when their country of Krisna is invaded by an army led by Zess, the fourth member of their old circle (Manga Bookshelf). Complete in 20 volumes; adapted to anime films (MU).
life_message: Loyalty to friends and the courage to fight for them matter even when war turns old friends into enemies.

content.note: Full-scale invasion and mecha battles (Titan blurb; Manga Bookshelf); AniList War; MU Large Scale Battles.
Surrender terms would execute the royal family (Manga Bookshelf); AniList Tragedy (spoiler).
Sigyn's unrequited feelings for Rygart (Manga Bookshelf); MU Marriage Without Love, Romantic Subplot.
MU lists Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (to verify).

dominant: Friendship and conflicting loyalties in war; an outcast's worth

frames.aligns: Rygart defends his friends and country; war's tragedy between old friends.
War shown as grief, friends turned enemies.
Faithfulness to friends and lawful rulers.
frames.concerns: Battle violence; quartz 'sorcery' is mostly technological.

frames.aligns: An overlooked man used for great purpose.
Serving one's neighbor and king in a hard calling.

frames.concerns: Mecha combat is the main spectacle.

frames.aligns: Shows war's human cost among friends.
Kshatriya-like duty against kin turned enemy, as in the Gita.
War born of grievance shown as suffering.
Shows futility of human governments' wars.
Worth of the one who lacks the common gift.
Harmony among friends; respect for ancient things.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Zess's grudge and personal rivalries alongside state war (Manga Bookshelf).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Military duty and royal command shape Rygart's choices.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Loyalty to a close circle of friends drives him (Manga Bookshelf).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Monarchy and military ranks accepted (MU Royalty, Military).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Technology-based world; ancient golem as relic.

folkways.japan: School-friend bonds that persist into adult rank and loyalty reflect Japanese emphasis on old classmates and duty.

delivery.evidence: Manga Bookshelf: war framed through personal relationships, not political commentary; not called preachy.
delivery.note: The invading leader Zess is an old friend with his own grievances, so the opposing side is drawn with some sympathy (to verify).

winners_losers: Sympathy lies with Rygart and the friends he defends; Zess's side is drawn as human rather than evil. Final outcome not in sources.
to_verify: Graphic level of later battles and deaths
Whether the invaders' cause is given a fair case
